Subject: Re: Intermittent p99 spikes on long-context batch runs (32k) — initial findings & mitigation plan

Sara — thanks for the artifacts, they were very helpful. Preliminary findings from the first-pass analysis (ingest -> runtime traces):

Summary: p95 shows minor uplift (~5-10%) but p99 regressed significantly and aligns with periods of concurrent large-context requests. We see two correlated signals:
- KV-cache churn: long-context requests (~32k) are causing frequent KV eviction/repopulation under sustained concurrency, producing tail latency for requests that suffer cache misses mid-stream.
- Batch head-of-line blocking: the serving runtime's continuous-batching heuristic is occasionally forming mixed-size batches where a single 32k request holds the batch open for additional microseconds, amplifying p99 for co-batched smaller requests.

Evidence & links:
- Live dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenant/pathway/latency?range=6h
- Capture: profile_32k_capture.json shows KV miss bursts at ~12:14:32 and 12:33:07 (UTC).
- JIRA: JIRA-INC-3421 created to track the incident and mitigation work.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (low-risk, can be rolled back quickly):
1) Soft rate-limit for >16k context requests during your nightly window (configurable threshold) — reduces concurrency pressure on KV cache.
2) Route long-context requests to a quantized 16k-compatible model variant with prefix stitching (decreases per-token kernel pressure).
3) Batch-splitting: ensure continuous batching separates large-context requests into isolated batches when concurrency threshold exceeded.

Planned next steps (SRE):
- Hour 1: apply soft rate-limit and enable batch-splitting rule (monitoring-only).
- Hour 2-4: measure impact; if p99 improves, consider routing policy for longer-term stability.

Risks: routing to 16k variant will change output fidelity slightly for extreme-long prompts — requires Pathway sign-off.

I'll push an internal runbook into the JIRA ticket and start the mitigation work now. Please confirm whether Pathway wants us to apply routing or just rate-limit first.

— Marissa Cole | Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Impact: customer nightly runs delayed by up to 8–12s at p99; 500s observed for a subset of requests resulting in downstream pipeline failures. They reported ~120 RPS sustained across their window; this is a high-value tenant with an expansion in negotiation (Q4).

Recommended immediate actions for exec approval:
1) Authorize a goodwill credit for the impacted window (Ben to propose amount).
2) Approve emergency routing to a 16k-compatible variant (temporary SLA exception if needed) while SRE applies longer-term fixes (KV/caching and batching improvements).
3) Prioritize JIRA-INC-3421 in the on-call queue for next 72 hours and allocate a small engineering task force (SRE + runtime engineering).

Asks: Vivek — please confirm approval for (1) and (2) so we can communicate to Pathway and act within the next hour.

I'll include a one-page exec note for the board if we need to escalate further.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu | Account Executive
